short: An American ultra-high-altitude reconnaissance aircraft that provided critical intelligence throughout the Cold War.
full:
Entering service in 1956, the Lockheed U-2 "Dragon Lady" was designed to fly deep into Soviet airspace at altitudes exceeding 70,000 feet, well above the reach of contemporary fighters and anti-aircraft missiles. Functioning effectively as a powered glider with jet engines, its long, narrow wings allowed it to carry heavy optical and electronic sensors to the edge of space. Its intelligence gathering revealed vital information about Soviet bomber and missile capabilities, significantly shaping American strategic policy.

The U-2 gained international infamy in 1960 when Francis Gary Powers was shot down over the Soviet Union, and again in 1962 when U-2 imagery sparked the Cuban Missile Crisis. Despite its vulnerability to modern surface-to-air missiles, continuous sensor upgrades have kept the aircraft highly relevant for high-altitude tactical reconnaissance into the present day.
